tasks.short: Instruct patients in therapeutic activities and techniques

steps.what: Retrieve and check the patient's current approved activity plan, restrictions and relevant vetted activity instructions in the clinical record system
inputs: Existing approved patient activity plan and restrictions

steps.what: Instruct the patient in the actual sports, dance, music, art or relaxation activity, demonstrate techniques and adapt instruction to their needs and response
outputs: Patient instruction and actual observed response

tasks.design: Use the patient-linked approved-plan and activity-instruction view in the clinical {OPS_SYSTEM}. The therapist still instructs and demonstrates techniques and responds to the actual patient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current restrictions and vetted activity instructions may require separate navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing patient-linked views can bring those sources together without generating treatment advice.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting instruction to physical and psychological needs and actual participation.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist observes and responds to the patient in real time.

ambition.what: Reduce approved-source retrieval effort within personal instruction.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3; clinical record owner approves therapist access and vetted instruction links

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical record views can link an approved patient activity plan and vetted instruction material.

assumptions: The responsible clinical team supplies an existing approved plan and restrictions; the provider supplies vetted instructions. s1 checks currency and gaps, with missing information returned to the clinical team.

Actual participation observation and required session documentation are explicitly modeled in task 387 and counted once if this is the same session; they are not a free automated note hidden in instruction.
No new record, patient message or treatment recommendation is generated in this instruction step.
Illustrative gross saving 2 per 100 task hours, upkeep 0.5, net 1.5; existing equivalent views earn no new gain and live instruction remains fully counted.
unknowns: Actual retrieval effort and current patient-linked instruction views
research_questions: Can the therapist see the current approved restrictions and activity instructions together today?

already_counted.description: Check approved patient and instruction sources

incremental.description: Maintain approved activity links and view fields

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Unmeasured instruction episode; only source navigation reduced, session documentation counted in its own task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan, organize and deliver therapeutic recreation programs

steps.what: Plan the actual rehabilitation and community-integration activities from the approved treatment objectives and patient needs
inputs: Actual approved treatment objectives and patient needs

steps.what: Retrieve and check actual room, staff and activity-resource availability in the provider's existing scheduling view
inputs: Existing staff-entered calendars and resource availability
outputs: Checked feasible activity arrangements and conflicts

steps.what: Enter and check the actual chosen program schedule, patient group and resource arrangements in the existing program record
inputs: Checked arrangements and actual selected participants

steps.what: Save the final checked program schedule in the same program system
Organize the actual session, direct and participate in activities, support community participation and adapt delivery to patients' actual responses
inputs: Actual patients, activity resources and approved program
outputs: Delivered therapeutic recreation activities and observed patient response

tasks.design: Configure an actual availability view and reusable program fields in {CALENDAR} and the clinical program {OPS_SYSTEM}. The therapist chooses the activities and arrangements, checks the final schedule and retains actual organization, direction and participation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability lookup and repeating program identifiers can add logistical handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling views and program forms can reuse current records.
tasks.still_hard: Patient suitability, safe participation and changing needs during activities.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist adapts actual delivery to patients and their community context.

ambition.what: Reduce existing program scheduling and recording effort.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3; clinical and scheduling owners confirm permitted patient and resource views

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: scheduling systems can show actual resource availability and linked program forms can reuse existing identifiers.

assumptions: Staff and resource owners maintain actual availability records; s2 checks conflicts and gaps and s3 captures the therapist's real arrangement decisions. No free transport, venue booking or external partner acceptance is assumed.
This episode already includes an internal program schedule; saving it sends no hidden invitation or notification. Any actual external booking requires its own checked final request and send step.
Treatment-plan development is counted in task 388 and participation documentation in task 387; shared work is counted once.
Illustrative gross saving 6.3 per 100 task hours, upkeep 1.5, net 4.8; actual delivery and same-system save earn no gain.
unknowns: Actual scheduling workload and current availability view coverage
research_questions: Which program fields and availability checks are repeated manually today?

already_counted.description: Check availability and capture and check actual schedule choices

incremental.description: Maintain program fields and availability links

approvals.approved_version: Final program schedule and participants checked in s3; edits require rechecking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Unmeasured internally scheduled program episode; logistics navigation and repeated fields reduced after upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe, analyze and record participation and modify treatment

steps.what: Observe and analyze patients' actual participation, reactions and progress during the treatment session and judge whether treatment needs modification
outputs: Actual observations and therapist's clinical interpretation

steps.what: Capture actual observed facts, progress and therapist-decided treatment modifications in brief clinical source notes
inputs: Actual observations and clinical interpretation from s1
outputs: Therapist-authored source facts and explicit modification decisions

steps.what: Draft the session narrative and wording of the therapist's decided plan changes from the captured clinical facts
inputs: Therapist-authored source facts and explicit decisions from s2
outputs: Draft session note and draft plan-change wording

loop.purpose: Express captured session facts and therapist-decided modifications in the record's required narrative form
loop.input: Actual therapist-authored source facts and explicit modification decisions
loop.output: Draft session narrative and plan-change wording without new treatment recommendations
loop.check: Therapist checks every clinical fact, omission, patient identity and plan change against actual observations and decisions in s4
loop.stop: Missing fact, conflicting source or new inferred treatment returns to therapist; no authentication or plan write
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative synthesis requires meaning; direct structured field reuse uses native forms first

steps.what: Correct and clinically check the complete session note and exact treatment-program change against actual observations and professional authority
inputs: Complete draft note and plan change
Actual source facts, existing plan and therapist decisions
outputs: Final checked session note and exact authorized plan-change version

steps.what: Authenticate the final checked session note in the same clinical record system
Commit the exact checked and authorized treatment-program modification in the same clinical record system

tasks.design: Capture actual session facts in the clinical {OPS_SYSTEM}, then use a bounded drafting step for narrative and wording of the therapist's explicit plan decisions. The therapist checks both complete versions before separate note authentication and treatment-program commits.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning actual observations and decisions into complete clinical prose can duplicate captured information.
tasks.enabler_now: A provider-approved draft helper can express supplied facts while the clinician retains all clinical decisions and final checks.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting participation and deciding if and how treatment should change.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist observes actual patients and takes responsibility for clinical interpretation and changes.

ambition.what: Reduce clinical prose drafting while retaining observation, capture, judgment and authentication.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-6; provider approves clinical-data handling, draft-tool use and treatment-change authority

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded clinical-note drafting can express supplied observations for complete clinician review without choosing treatment.

assumptions: The therapist observes patients and captures actual source facts and explicit modification decisions in s1-s2; no ambient transcript, clean clinical feed or invented observation is assumed.
The draft helper may change wording only, never infer progress, prescribe activity or modify treatment. Missing clinical facts stop drafting.

This episode concerns modifications within the therapist's actual existing authority; a change needing another practitioner's approval waits for that actual approval after its exact final version exists.
Illustrative gross saving 9 per 100 task hours, upkeep 2.5, net 6.5. Both same-system commits remain fully retained and earn no gain.
Count actual observation and record work once if shared with tasks 393, 395 or 388; no separate duplicate session report is added.
unknowns: Actual narrative-writing effort and provider-approved drafting capability
research_questions: How much session-note effort remains after actual observations are captured, and which plan changes require another practitioner?

already_counted.description: Capture actual clinical facts, review the draft and clinically check both final versions

incremental.description: Review draft omissions and maintain note and plan-wording templates

approvals.approved_version: Final session note clinically checked in s4; edits require rechecking
Exact authorized treatment-program change checked in s4; edits require rechecking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Unmeasured clinical narrative scenario; actual observation, source capture, clinical decisions and full final checks retained, upkeep deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop a patient-specific recreational treatment plan

steps.what: Retrieve and check the actual needs assessment, therapy objectives, restrictions and relevant clinical history in the patient record
inputs: Actual existing needs assessment and clinical records
outputs: Checked assessment basis and missing information

steps.what: Discuss the patient's actual interests, preferences and participation constraints and clarify assessment gaps
outputs: Actual interests and clarified needs or unresolved gaps

steps.what: Develop and record the actual patient-specific treatment goals, activities, adaptations and review criteria from clinical judgment
inputs: Actual needs, interests, restrictions and objectives

steps.what: Draft and edit the treatment-plan prose from the therapist's actual decisions in the provider's plan template
inputs: Therapist-authored decisions and rationale from s3
Actual captured patient interests and clinical facts

loop.purpose: Express the therapist's already made plan decisions in the required document structure
loop.input: Actual therapist-authored goals, activities, adaptations, review criteria and source facts
loop.output: Draft plan prose without new clinical recommendations
loop.check: Therapist checks every goal, activity, restriction and patient fact against actual decisions and sources in s5
loop.stop: Unsupported activity, missing source or altered restriction returns to therapist; no plan save
loop.why_not_simpler: Individual narrative wording requires semantic drafting; fixed headings and structured fields use native templates first

steps.what: Correct and clinically check the complete final treatment plan, patient identity, restrictions, feasibility and actual approval status
inputs: Actual source records and therapist decisions
outputs: Final checked treatment-plan version within existing authority

steps.what: Save the final checked treatment-plan version in the same clinical record system
outputs: Saved treatment-plan version with actual approval status

tasks.design: Use the patient-linked assessment view and plan template in the clinical {OPS_SYSTEM}, with bounded prose drafting only after the therapist has developed the actual plan. The therapist checks the complete final version before saving it with its real approval status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assessment-source navigation and turning explicit plan decisions into prose can repeat effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record views and a provider-approved draft helper can assist those bounded operations.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing suitable therapeutic activities and realistic goals for the actual patient.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist combines the patient's interests with clinical needs and professional judgment.

ambition.what: Reduce source retrieval and actual plan prose drafting without automating treatment choice.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-6; provider approves clinical inputs, draft use and actual plan authority

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: patient-linked record views and bounded drafting can assist documentation of clinician-authored treatment plans.

assumptions: An actual needs assessment is supplied by its real clinical producer; its assessment labor is counted there. s1 checks its content and s2 captures actual patient interests and gaps.
The therapist makes and records all treatment decisions in s3. No clean patient preference profile, free transcript or model recommendation is assumed.

The saved version retains the provider's actual approval status; if medical authorization is still required it remains a working plan pending review of this exact final version, not released treatment.
Illustrative gross saving 12 per 100 task hours, upkeep 3, net 9; same-system save earns no gain. Any shared plan change or source lookup with task 387 is counted once.
unknowns: Actual plan-authority process and prose-writing effort
research_questions: Which plan content is already structured and which prose still repeats the therapist's explicit decisions?

already_counted.description: Check assessment sources, formulate plan decisions, review drafted prose and clinically check the complete version

incremental.description: Maintain plan template and review draft fidelity and omissions

approvals.approved_version: Complete treatment-plan version and actual approval status checked in s5; edits require rechecking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Unmeasured plan-documentation scenario; actual needs capture, treatment decisions and complete clinical checks retained, upkeep deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: Use provider-approved clinical-record views and templates with actual assessment producers and treatment authorities.
skills_to_grow: Check bounded clinical prose for omissions
role.ambitious_version: A recreational therapist who spends less time locating records and expressing already made decisions while retaining patient instruction, observation, therapeutic judgment and clinical responsibility.
